page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-64 is a flexible compute instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory. This distribution establishes a 1:2 core-to-memory profile of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU, aligning the instance with compute-intensive tasks that require substantial processing density without excessive memory overhead.

The server contains no bundled local storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs, operating exclusively with network-attached block volumes for persistent storage requirements. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the underlying hardware provides dedicated physical compute execution, thread contention is minimized compared to burstable or shared-core platforms. However, relying entirely on network block storage requires planning around external volume bandwidth for I/O operations.

VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-64 delivers cost efficiency for compute-skewed operations by avoiding the overhead of unneeded memory capacity. Workloads aligned with this resource profile include continuous integration and deployment runners, multi-threaded software build systems, batch compute jobs, and distributed application services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-64 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at 2.55 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage attachments for persistent data needs. Network allocation features one complimentary public IPv4 address. Dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute execution for concurrent processing tasks without shared virtualization interference. VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-64 fits compute-focused tasks requiring dense multi-threading without oversized memory allocations, including software compilation pipelines, batch processing, and scalable application hosting.
